instructions: On Sunday, or up to 3 days ahead: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk the 1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup cocoa, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt.
In a large bowl, mash the banana, then whisk in the 2 eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup milk, 2 tsp oil and 1 tsp vanilla.
Shred the zucchini on the big holes of a box grater, then squeeze out the extra water in a clean towel. That should be about 1 cup.
Stir the flour mix into the wet bowl until just combined. Fold in the zucchini and 1/4 cup of the chocolate chips. Stop as soon as there's no dry flour left.
Divide the batter among the 12 cups and sprinkle the remaining 1/4 cup chips over the tops.
Bake for 23 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool the muffins completely in the tin before you move them. This makes 12 muffins.
Counter or fridge: keep them in a sealed container for up to 4 days, in the fridge if your kitchen is warm.
Freezer: wrap the cooled muffins one at a time and freeze them in a bag for up to 2 months.
In the morning, warm a muffin in the microwave for 20 to 30 seconds. For a frozen one, microwave it for 45 to 60 seconds, until warm in the middle.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the whole batch on Sunday, or up to 3 days ahead, and keep the muffins on the counter, in the fridge or in the freezer.
method_notes: Our Zesty Life is the lead: whole wheat and cocoa, a mashed banana for sweetness and moisture, and chocolate chips folded in and sprinkled on top. It has 12 ratings, so this is a fallback. Its walnuts are left out to keep it nut-free. Little Sweet Baker says not to squeeze the zucchini, but this follows the lead and squeezes out the extra water. All the sources agree: shredded zucchini, cocoa, chips, and mix as little as you can.
